items.title: Warning signs: hazards ahead
items.simple: Yellow and black signs warn you that a hazard may be ahead. Slow down. Then watch for more signs, road markings, signals, or work zones.
items.official: Warning signs alert you to possible hazards ahead. Slow down and watch for other pavement markings, signs, signals or work zones that may follow.
items.mnemonic: Yellow and black means heads up: slow down.

items.title: Advisory speed: safe exit speed
items.simple: This yellow sign shows the top safe speed for a highway exit. Slow down to that speed before you take the exit.
items.official: Advisory Speed: This sign indicates the maximum safe speed for a highway exit.

items.title: Stop Ahead and Yield Ahead
items.simple: This yellow sign shows a small stop or yield sign. It means a real stop or yield sign is coming up. Slow down and get ready to stop.
items.official: Stop Ahead/Yield Ahead: A stop sign or yield sign is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.
items.mnemonic: Ahead means coming soon. Slow now, so you are ready.

items.title: Signal Ahead
items.simple: A yellow sign with a traffic light on it means traffic lights are ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.
items.official: Signal Ahead: Traffic signals are ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

items.title: No Passing Zone sign
items.simple: This yellow flag-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone. Do not pass cars ahead of you in your lane. Stay behind them, even when the road looks clear.
items.official: No Passing Zone: This sign marks the beginning of a no passing zone. You may not pass cars ahead of you in your lane, even if the way is clear.

items.title: Merge: two lanes become one
items.simple: Two lanes going the same way will soon become one lane. Drivers in BOTH lanes must merge safely.
items.official: Merge: Two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to become one. Drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging safely.
items.mnemonic: Merge is a team job. Both lanes share it.

items.title: Lane reduction: right lane ends
items.simple: The right lane ends soon. If you are in the right lane, move left when there is space. If you are in the left lane, let other cars merge in smoothly.
items.official: Lane Reduction: The right lane ends soon. Drivers in the right lane must merge left when space opens up. Drivers in the left lane should allow other vehicles to merge smoothly.
items.mnemonic: Right lane ends, so right lane bends left.

items.title: Divided highway begins or ends
items.simple: When a divided highway begins, a middle strip splits the road into two roadways. Each roadway goes one way. When the divided highway ends, there is no middle strip, and cars go both ways. In both cases, keep right.
items.official: Divided Highway Begins: The highway ahead is split into two separate roadways by a median or divider and each roadway is one-way. Keep right. Divided Highway Ends: The highway ahead no longer has a median or divider. Traffic goes in both directions. Keep right.
items.mnemonic: Begins or ends, the rule is the same: keep right.

items.title: Slippery When Wet
items.simple: When the road is wet, slow down. Do not brake hard or turn the wheel suddenly. Leave more space between you and the car ahead.
items.official: Slippery When Wet: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed. Do not brake hard or change direction suddenly. Increase the distance between your car and the one ahead of you.

items.title: Low Clearance
items.simple: The overpass ahead is low. The sign shows how much room is under it. If your vehicle is taller than that, do not go under it.
items.official: Low Clearance Sign: The overpass ahead has a low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

items.title: Hill: steep grade ahead
items.simple: A sign with a truck on a slope means a steep hill is ahead. Check your brakes.
items.official: Hill: A steep grade is ahead. Check your brakes.

items.title: Deer Crossing
items.simple: Deer cross the road in this area. Slow down. Stay alert. Be ready to stop.
items.official: Deer Crossing: Deer cross the roadway in this area. Slow down, be alert and be ready to stop.

items.title: Horse-drawn buggies: no horn
items.simple: Horse-drawn buggies often travel in this area. Slow down. Do not use your horn.
items.official: Horse-Drawn Buggies: Regularly travel in this area. Slow down and don't use the horn.
items.mnemonic: Horse and buggy: slow and quiet.

items.title: Pass buggies with 3 feet
items.simple: When you pass a horse-drawn buggy, leave at least 3 feet of space. Pass only when the way is clear.
items.official: State law requires motorists to pass with at least three feet of clearance when the way is clear.
items.mnemonic: Give a buggy a yardstick: 3 feet or more.

items.title: Tractors and farm equipment
items.simple: Tractors and farm machines often use this road. Be ready to slow down or stop. Pass only when the way is clear.
items.official: Tractors and Farm Equipment: Regularly travel in this area. Be ready to slow down or stop. Only pass when the way is clear.

items.title: Pedestrian Crossing
items.simple: Watch for people crossing. They may walk, ride bikes or use other devices. Slow down and be ready to stop. A second sign with an arrow may point to the crosswalk.
items.official: Pedestrian Crossing: Watch for people who are walking, riding bicycles or other devices entering a crosswalk or crossing your path. Slow down and be prepared to stop. A second sign with an arrow may show the actual location of the crosswalk.

items.title: Bicycle Crossing
items.simple: Bikes often cross the road or ride next to cars here. Drive with care. A second sign with an arrow may show where bikes cross.
items.official: Bicycle Crossing/Bike Path: Bicycles regularly cross or ride beside traffic in this area. Drive with caution. A second sign with an arrow may show the actual location of the bike crossing.

items.title: School Zone / School Crossing
items.simple: A five-sided sign with two kids means a school zone or crossing. Watch for children. Be ready to slow down or stop. Obey the speed limit and the crossing guards.
items.official: School Zone/School Crossing: Watch out for children crossing the street or playing. Be ready to slow down or stop at school zones and surrounding areas. Obey the speed limit and signals from crossing guards.

items.title: Open joints and expansion joints
items.simple: Joints are seams across the road on bridges or ramps. Slow down. Open joints can make a motorcycle rider lose control. Wide joints can make tires slip when the road is wet.
items.official: Open Joints: Slow down. Open joints on bridges or ramps could cause a motorcyclist to lose control of the motorcycle. Expansion Joints: This sign is used when a joint across lanes creates a bump or is wide enough to cause loss of traction in wet weather.

items.title: Intersection (crossroad) ahead
items.simple: A plus-shaped sign means a crossroad is ahead. Watch for cars coming onto your road.
items.official: Intersections: An intersection is ahead. Be alert for vehicles entering the road on which you are traveling.

items.title: Y Intersection
items.simple: A Y-shaped sign means the road splits ahead. You must bear right or left.
items.official: Y Intersection: You must bear either right or left ahead.

items.title: T Intersection
items.simple: A T-shaped sign means your road ends ahead at a stop sign. Let oncoming cars and people walking go first. Then turn right or left.
items.official: T Intersection: The roadway you are traveling on ends ahead at a stop sign. You must turn right or left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
items.mnemonic: T is for Turn: the road ends.

items.title: Roundabout ahead
items.simple: Arrows in a circle mean a roundabout is ahead. Yield to cars already in the circle. Then drive around the circle counterclockwise.
items.official: Roundabout: These signs indicate a circular intersection with an island in the center is ahead. Also called traffic circles, these intersections may have one or more lanes. Entering traffic must yield the right-of-way to traffic already in the circle and travel in a counter clockwise direction.
items.mnemonic: Circle cars go first. Then go around opposite the clock hands.

items.title: Right curve with side road
items.simple: The road curves right. A side road joins from the left inside the curve. Watch for cars coming onto your road.
items.official: Right Curve – Side Road: The road ahead curves right and a side road joins from the left within the curve. Be alert for vehicles entering the roadway you are traveling on.

items.title: Curve and sharp turn signs
items.simple: A smoothly bending arrow means a curve. A square-cornered arrow means a sharp turn. An arrow that goes right, then left, means the road bends right, then left. For all of them, slow down.
items.official: Sharp Right Turn: Slow down and be prepared for a sharp right turn in the road ahead. Sharp Right and Left Turns: Slow down and be prepared for the road ahead to turn sharply right, then left. Right and Left Curves: The road ahead curves right, then left. Slow down.

items.title: Curve with safe speed plaque
items.simple: The road curves right. The small sign under it shows the safe speed for the curve. Slow down to that speed.
items.official: Right Curve with Safe Speed Indicator: The road ahead curves right. Slow down to the safe speed indicated.

items.title: Winding Road
items.simple: A wiggly arrow means the road has many turns or curves in a row. On all curves, slow down so you stay in control.
items.official: Winding Road: The road ahead winds with a series of turns or curves. On all curves, slow down for better control.

items.title: Low ground railroad crossing
items.simple: The road has a steep slope where it crosses the train tracks. The bottom of a low vehicle can get caught or drag on the tracks.
items.official: Low Ground Railroad Crossing: A steep slope where the railroad tracks cross the road may cause the bottom of low vehicles to get caught or drag on the tracks.

items.title: Railroad advance warning sign
items.simple: A round yellow sign with an X and two R's comes before a railroad crossing. Look, listen, and slow down. Be ready to stop for trains.
items.official: Railroad Crossing: Advance warning signs are placed before a railroad crossing. These signs warn you to look, listen, slow down and be prepared to stop for trains or any vehicles using the rails.
items.mnemonic: Round RR sign: Look, Listen, Slow.

items.title: Railroad crossbuck
items.simple: A white X sign marks a railroad crossing. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Trains can come from either way. With two or more tracks, a train can be on any track.
items.official: Railroad Crossbuck: This sign is a warning of a railroad crossing. Look, listen, slow down and be prepared to stop for trains or any vehicles using the rails. If there is more than one track, trains may be approaching from either direction on either track.

items.title: Crossbuck with flashing lights
items.simple: When red lights start to flash, stop. Wait until the trains pass, the tracks are clear, and the lights stop flashing. If there is more than one track, another train may come.
items.official: Always stop when the light begins to flash and be alert for approaching trains. Do not proceed until all trains or any other vehicles using the rails have passed, the tracks are clear, and the lights are no longer flashing.

items.title: Railroad gate: never go around
items.simple: Stop when the lights start to flash, before the gate comes down. Stay stopped until the gates go up and the lights stop flashing. Never drive around a lowered gate.
items.official: Crossbuck, Flashing Lights and Gate: Stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers. Remain stopped until the gates are raised and the lights stop flashing. Do not attempt to drive around the lowered gate.
items.mnemonic: Gate down? Stay. Gate up and lights off? Go.

items.title: RR pavement marking
items.simple: If you see a big X and RR painted on the road, a railroad crossing is coming up. Be alert. Trains can come at any time, from either direction.
items.official: Pavement markings, consisting of an X and RR, may be painted on the pavement at the approach to some crossings. When approaching railroad tracks, be alert. Trains may approach the crossing at any time and from either direction.

items.title: Only cross if you can clear
items.simple: Never start across train tracks unless you can get all the way over. First make sure there is room for your car on the other side.
items.official: Unless you can clear the tracks completely, never start across the tracks. Make sure there is room for your vehicle on the other side of the tracks before proceeding.

items.title: School buses always stop at tracks
items.simple: School buses must always stop at railroad crossings. They stop even when the lights are not flashing. Expect the bus ahead of you to stop there.
items.official: Note: School buses must always stop at railroad crossings, even when the lights are not flashing.

items.title: Stalled on tracks: get out
items.simple: If your car stalls on the tracks, get out right away. Do not wait. Run away from the tracks at an angle. Head in the direction the train is coming from.
items.official: If your car stalls on the tracks, don't hesitate. Get out of the car right away and run diagonally away from the tracks in the direction of the oncoming train.
items.mnemonic: Stalled? Get out. Run at an angle toward the train.

items.title: Rail danger: call posted number
items.simple: If you see something dangerous at a rail crossing, call the number on the emergency sign. When you call, give the crossing number posted there. Then the railroad can stop or reroute trains.
items.official: If a dangerous condition exists at a rail crossing, call the number listed on the emergency sign. This will allow the rail company to stop or reroute approaching rail traffic until the hazard is removed. Be sure to give the posted crossing number so that the hazard can be identified correctly.
